title: Best Purchase Order Financing Companies (2026)
summary: Compare purchase order financing companies and bank alternatives for 2026. Review vendor payments, eligibility, repayment terms and questions to ask lenders.
body_markdown:
Photo:[Vida Huang / Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/warehouse-storage-filled-with-pallets-of-goods-I-_wYj9yOzw) .


The best **purchase order financing companies** for your business depend on the order you need to fund. This guide compares Drip Capital, SouthStar Capital, Liquid Capital and King Trade Capital, alongside five banks offering loans or credit lines that can help fund purchases. Order size, available margin and the vendor’s payment deadline should shape your shortlist.


A confirmed customer order can still leave you with a cash gap. Some funders pay the vendor and collect repayment through the customer’s invoice; others give you a separate repayment schedule. Check the structure before comparing the price.


## **Best Purchase Order Financing Companies (2026): The List**


We reviewed the providers’ published product descriptions on November 23, 2026. The list is an editorial comparison, rather than a measured ranking. The banks below offer alternatives to transaction-specific PO funding. Ask each provider for a written quote and eligibility review.


### **1. Drip Capital**


Drip Capital’s[Vendor Financing](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/vendor-financing/) pays vendors directly, with repayment terms of up to 90 days, subject to approval and agreed terms. It can help established businesses pay for goods before collecting from their customers. Confirm the facility, supported purchases and repayment dates before committing to an order.


**Best for:** **established businesses that buy and sell goods and need a vendor paid to fill an order.**


### **2. SouthStar Capital**


SouthStar Capital advertises financing for up to 100% of purchase-order costs. Its process covers fulfilllment and transitions to Accounts Receivable Financing once the goods are delivered and invoiced. Ask for the charges and repayment conditions at both stages.


**Best for:** **distributors, wholesalers, importers and manufacturers with large orders and limited working capital.**


### **3. Liquid Capital**


**Liquid Capital covers up to 100% of the cost of product in transit once approved, for companies buying finished or near-finished goods and selling to creditworthy customers. Businesses incorporated in the United States or Canada may qualify. It works through locally owned principals and typically pairs PO financing with its own factoring, which pays off the PO advance. Fees are not published.**


**Best for:** **product businesses that want PO funding and factoring from one provider.**


### **4. King Trade Capital**


King Trade Capital finances purchase orders and trade cycles, including government contracts. It requires a proven track record and says it does not finance startups. Its funding-request page specifies a minimum of $3 million in annual finance utilization; check that requirement before applying.


**Best for:** **established companies with large commercial or government orders.**


### **5. Live Oak Bank**


Live Oak Bank offers SBA 7(a) loans of up to $5 million, including working-capital uses. Its published process includes underwriting and closing, so leave time to supply financial records and resolve questions. Ask whether the loan can support the purchases you have planned.


Best for: businesses planning working-capital needs ahead of a vendor deadline.


### **6. Huntington**


Huntington offers SBA-backed financing and participates in the SBA Preferred Lender Program. Compare the proposed use of funds, repayment period and closing requirements with the length of your order cycle.


Best for: businesses looking for an SBA lending relationship.


### **7. JPMorgan Chase**


Chase offers a business Line of Credit for managing cash flow and growth. A revolving facility may suit repeat purchases, but approval, available credit and the draw terms still need to fit your buying schedule.


Best for: businesses comparing revolving bank credit for recurring purchases.


### **8. Bank of America**


Bank of America offers an unsecured Business Advantage Credit Line. Ask about eligibility, the approved limit, renewal conditions and all fees before treating it as the funding source for your next order.


**Best for:** **smaller, established businesses that want an unsecured line.**


### **9. Wells Fargo**


Wells Fargo offers BusinessLine, an unsecured revolving business Line of Credit. A bank line can support recurring cash needs within its approved terms; confirm that the amount and repayment structure suit your purchases.


Best for: businesses seeking revolving bank credit for ongoing operations.


## **How Purchase Order Financing Works**


A **purchase order financing company** reviews your customer order, vendor costs and ability to deliver. If approved, it funds agreed costs. Some arrangements then move into Invoice Financing after delivery. Review both stages in the[Purchase Order Financing guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/finance-guides/purchase-order-financing) .


Before applying, confirm what happens if the customer disputes the shipment, the vendor delivers late or the order is canceled. Our[PO financing requirements guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/who-qualifies-for-purchase-order-financing-requirements-and-how-to-get-approved) explains the information funders may review.


## **What Purchase Order Financing Costs**


Compare **PO financing companies** using the total amount payable for your expected funding period. Ask how fees accrue, whether partial periods are charged in full, and whether factoring, inspection, wire or other charges are separate. A headline percentage alone does not answer those questions.


Prepare two quotes: one using your expected delivery and payment dates, and another allowing for a delay. Check how much profit remains after goods, freight, duties and financing. This gives you a more useful comparison than choosing the lowest advertised rate.


A bank line or SBA-backed loan may also fit. Compare the full cost and the date funds will actually be available, then match the repayment schedule to your cash-flow plan.


## **How to Choose a Purchase Order Funding Company**


**The** **best purchase order financing companies** **for you fund your type of goods, order size and customers. Ask every provider:**


- **What share of the vendor's cost do you advance, and do you pay the vendor directly?**
- **What is the fee per 30 days, and how is it charged after that?**
- **Is there a minimum deal size or an annual minimum?**
- **Do you need a personal guarantee or collateral?**
- **Will you contact my customer, and what happens if they pay late?**


Compare **purchase order funding companies** on the full cost across your expected payment timeline. Ask for the same delay scenario in each quote.


## **Alternatives When PO Financing Doesn't Fit**


The[SBA Working Capital Pilot](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/trade-tools-for-international-sales/) supports lines of up to $5 million for domestic and export working-capital needs. It can be structured around specific contracts or advances against inventory and receivables. A participating lender must approve the business and facility.


For export orders, SBA’s Export Working Capital Program also allows loans of up to $5 million. Ask a participating lender which program fits your order and when funds could become available.


## **How to Check a Lender Before You Sign**


**Free tools help you vet** **PO funding companies** **and banks. SBA's**[Lender Match](https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/loans/lender-match) **connects you with SBA lenders, and its**[lender activity reports](https://data.sba.gov/dataset/7a-504-activity-reports-fy2025-year-end) **show how many 7(a) loans each bank approved. Then ask the** **purchase order financing companies** **on your shortlist for a sample agreement and a written fee schedule before you share customer details.**


## **How Drip Capital Funds Purchase Orders**


Drip Capital pays vendors directly through[Vendor Financing](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/vendor-financing/) , helping businesses manage the gap between buying goods and collecting customer payments. Repayment terms are up to 90 days, subject to approval and agreed terms. Confirm your repayment schedule independently of the date your customer expects to pay.


**To check your next order,**[explore purchase order financing](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/purchase-order-financing/) **or**[apply online](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/apply) **.**


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What are the best purchase order financing companies in 2026?**


**Strong options include Drip Capital, SouthStar Capital, Liquid Capital and King Trade Capital for order-by-order funding, plus SBA lenders Live Oak Bank and Huntington and banks such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo for loans and credit lines. The best fit depends on your order size, margin, customer and how quickly your vendor needs payment.**


### **How much does purchase order financing cost?**


Pricing depends on the provider, order and financing period. Request a written total-cost example that includes any transition into Invoice Financing and the effect of a delayed shipment or payment.


### **Can a startup get purchase order financing?**


Requirements vary. King Trade Capital says it does not finance startups, while other providers assess different business and transaction criteria. Confirm operating-history requirements before spending time on an application.


### **What is the difference between PO financing and invoice factoring?**


Purchase Order Financing helps fund the costs of fulfillling an order. Invoice factoring involves selling an unpaid invoice after the sale; other Receivables Financing arrangements may instead involve borrowing against invoices. Some providers combine the stages, so review both agreements.


### **Do banks offer purchase order financing?**


Banks can support purchases through business credit lines, SBA-backed loans and trade-finance products. Ask whether the proposed facility funds your specific costs and is available before your vendor’s deadline.


### **What profit margin do I need for PO financing?**


There is no single margin requirement across all providers. Calculate the profit left after goods, freight, duties and the complete financing cost, then test a delayed-payment scenario before accepting terms.


### **How fast can I get purchase order financing?**


Timing depends on underwriting, documents and the transaction. Ask for separate dates for the credit decision, completion of conditions and vendor payment. A fast initial decision does not establish when the purchase will be funded.
